''See also: [[Titan Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|The term Titan refers to several distinct entities within the setting. Most prominently, the [[Wandering Titan]] is a massive, ancient creature often described as resembling a giant turtle with human-like features, such as five-fingered hands and a tail similar to a monkey's. It is characterized by its immense scale, appearing as part of the landscape with a shell the size of an island or hill. Known for its lethargy and inevitability rather than speed, it wanders the world to feed on minerals, [[earth aura]], and various forms of power like [[soulfire]] and [[madra]]. It is considered one of the [[Dreadgods]] and possesses enough strength to strain the fabric of space and upend heavens and earth. In a different context, [[Titans]] are also a group of individuals associated with the [[Abidan]]. These beings serve specific roles, such as maintaining protective barriers or claiming certain worlds like [[Threshold]] for reclamation. They are ranked by stars and possess unique physical traits, such as golden skin or specific heights, and they utilize specialized techniques to fulfill their duties.}}

== Relationships ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|Ruby can feel this being, while [[Yerin]] requires assistance to stop it. [[Northstrider]] keeps a constant gaze on the entity, and [[Lindon]] seeks to stall it using his [[advancement]]. [[Akura Malice]] attempted to push the being away, and the [[Hollow King]]'s Spear moved its arm. Additionally, [[Mercy]] and others are required to face this threat, while [[Judge Suriel{{!}}Suriel]] requests a connection to it. The [[Silent King]] discovered a method to swap places with the entity, and [[Lindon]] was stomped by its foot.}}

=== {{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|The battle at Mount Venture}} ===
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|[[Judge Suriel|Suriel]] requested a connection to the Titan, a being whose location is monitored by the [[Dreadgods]].<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c3">''Reaper'', chapter 3</ref><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c5">''Reaper'', chapter 5</ref> As a Titan was approaching awakening, its potential attack may have altered the [[suppression field]]'s power source or caused it to decay naturally through damage.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c5" /><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c8">''Reaper'', chapter 8</ref><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c9">''Reaper'', chapter 9</ref> This stone entity, known as [[Gadrael]], utilizes a molten shield to defend against void-beasts.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c12">''Reaper'', chapter 12</ref><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c15">''Reaper'', chapter 15</ref> The defense of the Titan serves to maintain the barrier on [[Cradle]].<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c26">''Reaper'', chapter 26</ref>}}

=== {{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Defense of Cradle}} ===
{{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Considered the least intelligent of the [[Dreadgods]], the Titan is characterized by its blazing yellow eyes.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c6">''Dreadgod'', chapter 6</ref> The entity possesses a [[hunger]] and exerts a [[Spiritual pressure|spiritual pressure]] capable of slowing the flow of [[madra]].<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c6" /> After displacing people within the city, the Titan demonstrated its ability to arrive directly by traveling through space.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c8">''Dreadgod'', chapter 8</ref><ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c10">''Dreadgod'', chapter 10</ref> The creature created a void [[portal]], though the [[Silent King]] eventually discovered how to swap places with it.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c16">''Dreadgod'', chapter 16</ref><ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c18">''Dreadgod'', chapter 18</ref>}}

=== {{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|Legacy of the Titans}} ===
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|Titan serves as one of the common aptitudes possessed by ascendants originating from [[Cradle]].<ref name="cradle-13-threshold-c4">''Threshold: Stories from Cradle'', chapter 4</ref> These [[Titans]] maintain a specific sense of claim over [[Threshold]], a connection reflected in [[Cirian]]'s own identification with them.<ref name="cradle-13-threshold-c7">''Threshold: Stories from Cradle'', chapter 7</ref>}}
